title: Create src/lib/parser/tags.ts — exit tag detection
description: Create a module to detect the three exit tags in AI output: <complete>, <blocked>reason</blocked>, and <decide>question</decide>. Each returns a typed result or null if the tag is not found.
acceptanceCriteria: detectComplete(text) returns true when <complete> is anywhere in text
detectComplete returns false for text without <complete>
detectBlocked('<blocked>reason</blocked>') extracts and returns the reason string
detectBlocked returns null when no blocked tag is found
detectDecide('<decide>question</decide>') extracts and returns the question string
detectDecide returns null when no decide tag is found

steps.details: Create the file with three exported functions.
export function detectComplete(text: string): boolean { return text.includes('<complete>') }

export function detectBlocked(text: string): { blocked: true; reason: string } | null { const match = text.match(/<blocked>(.*?)<\/blocked>/s); if (!match) return null; return { blocked: true, reason: match[1].trim() } }. The /s flag enables dotAll mode so . matches newlines.

export function detectDecide(text: string): { decide: true; question: string } | null { const match = text.match(/<decide>(.*?)<\/decide>/s); if (!match) return null; return { decide: true, question: match[1].trim() } }

technicalNotes: The /s flag (dotAll) in the regex allows . to match newlines — important for multi-line blocked reasons
detectComplete uses includes() not regex for simplicity — <complete> is a self-closing tag with no content
These functions should be called on the accumulated full output of each iteration, not individual lines
